who: JUAN CARLOS LERENA and MARIA LERENA
why: *** THE TWO THIS ARCHIVE EXISTS TO FIND, and the reason the red lane is drawn broken. *** They are named as the parents on Pablo Armando's army enrolment card and appear in NO OTHER RECORD ANYWHERE - not in Rosario, not in Montevideo, not in the full-text corpus. Every lane above is a candidate and none has been shown to hold them.

who: The LERENA LARRIERA of San Jose
why: *** TESTED AND EXCLUDED, 14 September 2026. *** Nine people, children of ALBERTO LERENA and MARIA INES LARRIERA. Zelmira Carlota was followed to her marriage in 1901 and her death in 1945, and the row says plainly: "she is NOT ours". *** A worked negative is worth as much as a lane. ***

who: The LARENA of Cayasta and Gualeguaychu
why: Nineteen people under the A-spelling, in the two Argentine provinces either side of the Parana. *** THE SPELLING IS NOT THE PROBLEM - this archive has catalogued LERENA read as SERENA, LORENA, LESINA and six more. *** What is missing is any document joining them to a Uruguayan house.

Married ADELA CAMIGLIA; a son AVELINO CARLOS born 1904. *** The forename AVELINO is the one that runs through Sancho's house ***, which is suggestive and is not evidence. Worked in September and not joined.

who: The LERENA of Trinidad with no father named
why: CAYETANA FAUSTINA, whose son Luis was registered in 1895 with no father on the act; RODOLFO BERNARDO and ISMAEL, each a father who appears once. *** Real people on real acts, attached to nobody. ***
Four people - Anna, Annunziata, Laurensa, Savina, Domenico, Paolo. *** An Italian name that is not a spelling of this one ***, kept in the register so that nobody has to discover them twice.

Felipa, Pedro and Isidoro Lerena in the parish marriages of Chuquibamba, Condesuyos. *** Found while searching the full-text corpus and recorded because a rare name in a far place is exactly what a careless session would merge. ***
One full-text hit in the Colombian Catholic records. *** Not pursued and not ours. ***

who: The LERENA y LERENA of Navarrete
why: *** A WHOLE HOUSEHOLD WHO CARRY THE NAME TWICE, and the most useful namesake on this page. *** ISABELA LERENA y BASARAN, widow, of Navarrete in La Rioja; her sons JOSE DOLORES, married and the propietario at home, and PRUDENCIO BENITO and JUAN JOSE, bachelors and shop-assistants in Buenos Aires, who in November 1900 signed a power of attorney at the Spanish consulate putting the Spanish property in their mother's hands. *** WHY IT IS DRAWN HERE AND NOT ON A LANE: *** they are Spanish subjects out of Logrono, and every lane above is Banda Oriental stock documented from the 1790s. *** WHY IT IS DRAWN AT ALL: *** Pablo Armando's enrolment card names a JUAN CARLOS LERENA and a MARIA LERENA, and the easiest way to dismiss that card is to call the repeated surname a clerk's slip. *** AND THEY ARE THE SIXTH SUCH COUPLE THIS ARCHIVE HAS MET, NOT THE FIRST - a correction to what was written here first. *** The two Trinidad couples of 1894 and 1913, the 1911 dispensation, Alejandro, and Eloy x Felisa Lerena at San Jose de Flores in 1912 all came before them. *** SO THE CARD'S DOUBLE SURNAME WAS NEVER IN REAL DOUBT, AND NAVARRETE DOES NOT RESCUE IT. *** What Navarrete adds is different and smaller: it is the *** FIRST SUCH HOUSEHOLD OUTSIDE SOUTH AMERICA ***, the *** FIRST WHERE THE CHILDREN CARRY IT DOUBLED AS A SURNAME OF RECORD *** - 'Lerena y Lerena', in their own signatures, not just a coincidence of two parents - and the *** FIRST TIME THE PRACTICE HAS A PLACE ON A MAP *** that can be searched. It does not make them his - no connection is claimed, and the CEMLA arrivals suggest a steady traffic of young Riojan Lerena men into Buenos Aires shops that has nothing to do with Rosario de Santa Fe in 1882.

*** A Lerena household on the Brazilian border, found 12 October 2026 and not on any lane. *** Benito, b. about 1854, Oriental, a jornalero who could not sign his name; his wife Maria Cristina, b. about 1856, Brazilian, given no surname by the act; their daughter Anastasia LERENA, b. about 1877, married to the Brazilian soldier Honorio ALVAREZ. Artigas is a department this archive has never worked, and a family of the name sitting on the Brazil frontier with Brazilian-born children is a shape nothing here predicts. *** Found only because a LERENA father was asked against a SERENA mother - and the act turns out to say Lerena both times. ***

where: Jesus Maria and Mal Abrigo, San Jose, Uruguay, 1910
why: *** An Italian-born Lerena in the department this archive rests an 1846 couple on. *** Pedro, b. about 1842 in Italy, a labrador; Juana Camacho, b. about 1853, Oriental; their daughter Ramona LERENA, b. about 1886, who registered a natural daughter Antonina at Mal Abrigo in September 1910 with the father's line left as se ignora. *** Kept here rather than on a lane, and kept as UNPLACED rather than as a namesake, because the honest position is that this archive cannot yet tell which stock he belongs to - which is itself the finding. *** /name/ separates an Italian Lerena/Lerina stock from this family; it has always been able to do that by country, and this act is the case where country does not decide.
